sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the request "Hashem is for me among my helpers" refers to drawing down the revelation of the name Havayah through the refinement of sparks, making the revelation internal and permanent through one's own effort.

translations.translation: And the point of the explanation in this
(in the maamar),
is that "my helpers" refers to the sparks that are refined through the service of man,
which are the helpers of man.
And the request "Hashem is for me among my helpers" is,
that through the service of refining the sparks
(my helpers)
"Hashem will be for me,"
that there will be drawn to him a revelation of the name Havayah that is above the chain of descent.
And it can be said,
that through the drawing down of the revelation of the name Havayah to the person
(Hashem is for me)
is through the refinement of the sparks
(among my helpers),
the revelation is in pnimiyus (inwardness).
For the revelation that is drawn to him from above in a manner of arousal from above by itself,
is in the aspect of makif (encompassing),
and therefore it has no permanence.
And so too regarding the drawing down that is drawn to him through his request in prayer.
Therefore it says "Hashem is for me among my helpers,"
that the drawing down of the revelation of the name Havayah to him is not in the manner of "bread of shame,"
but rather this
(as it were)
is coming to him for his service in the work of refinements,
the ultimate purpose of creation.
And through this "Hashem is for me" is effected,
that he becomes unified with the revelation,
so that the revelation is a thing that endures forever,
for wherever it says "for me," it never departs.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section discusses the two general types of spark refinement—through the service of tzaddikim and through repentance—and explains the superiority of refining permissible matters for the sake of Heaven.

translations.translation: And he continues with the verse "And I will see [my vengeance] upon my enemies,"
for in the refinement of sparks there are two matters in general.
The refinement of the sparks in the holy side through the service of the tzaddikim,
and the refinement of the sparks in the side of impurity through the service of repentance.
Therefore, in the place where penitents stand, even completely righteous tzaddikim cannot stand,

for the root of the sparks that fell into the side of impurity, which are refined by the penitent, is higher than the root of the sparks that fell into the holy side, which are refined by the tzaddikim.
And so too regarding the service of the tzaddikim
(and "all your people are tzaddikim"),
there is an advantage in the refinement of permissible matters through the service of "all your deeds should be for the sake of Heaven"
over the refinement of physical matters through the performance of mitzvos.
For since permissible matters,
even when one does them for the sake of Heaven, remain permissible matters
("your deeds"),
therefore,
through the refinement of permissible matters, the intention of a dwelling place in the lower realms is more fully completed,
a lower realm
than which there is no lower realm.
And therefore,
the ascent that is made in the soul through its descent below
[for the main ascent is through this, that in its descent below it completes the intention of a dwelling place in the lower realms]
is primarily through the refinement of permissible matters.
And this is "And I will see [my vengeance] upon my enemies,"
that through the refinement of the sparks in "my enemies"—the sparks in forbidden things,
and likewise the sparks in permissible matters,
which are also included in "my enemies" according to the well-known teaching of the Baal Shem Tov
on the verse
"When you see the donkey of your enemy"—they come to a vision of G‑dliness,
"and I will see."

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the concept of "I will see" includes not only refining permissible matters but also teaching Torah to others, which brings a higher form of assistance.

translations.translation: And 4)
Now, it is explained in many places
that the service of the tzaddikim is within themselves, and the matter of repentance is that a person also acts upon something external to himself and illuminates the world.
Based on this, it can be said,
that the matter of "I will see" in general is in addition to the refinement of permissible matters
(in "my enemies"),
but rather also through teaching Torah to another.
And as implied in the maamar
(of 12 Tammuz 5687)
regarding that which our sages said,
"One who comes to purify, they assist him,"
that the meaning of the language "to purify"
(and not "to become purified")
is to purify others,
it is,
for the help and assistance of the sparks that are refined
("they assist him" in the plural,
similar to "among my helpers")
when he comes to purify others, it is in a more elevated manner.
